raw: The purposes of this Act are— (a) to amend the Crimes Act 1958— (i) to increase the penalties by which certain offences are punishable; and (ii) to make it an offence to use a knife in the commission of any one of several specified indictable offences; and Victoria (iii) to provide that the theft of a vehicle is a carjacking if a child who is under the age of 10 is in the vehicle when it is stolen; and (b) to amend the Criminal Procedure Act 2009 to provide that the indictable offence of recruiting a child to engage in serious criminal activity may be heard and determined summarily (despite an increase to the penalty by which that offence is punishable); and (c) to amend the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 and the Youth Justice Act 2024— (i) to alter the matters to which a court must have regard when sentencing a child for an offence; and (ii) to make changes in relation to the charges that the Children's Court must not hear and determine summarily; and (d) to make consequential amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act 2009 and the Magistrates' Court Act 1989.

new: Division 2F—Use of knives in the commission of certain indictable offences 195X Use of knives in the commission of certain indictable offences (1) A person must not use a knife in committing a relevant offence. Penalty: 3 years imprisonment. (2) Each of the following is a relevant offence for the purposes of this section— (a) an offence against section 16 (causing serious injury intentionally); (b) an offence against section 17 (causing serious injury recklessly); (c) an offence against section 18 (causing injury intentionally or recklessly); (d) an offence against section 31(1) constituted by the conduct described in paragraph (a) of that provision (assaulting, or threatening to assault, with intent to commit an indictable offence); (e) an offence against section 195H (affray); (f) an offence against section 195I (violent disorder). (3) A person is not liable for an offence against subsection (1) unless the person is found guilty of the relevant offence referred to in that subsection. (4) Nothing in subsection (3) requires that a person must have been found guilty of a relevant offence before they may be charged with an offence against subsection (1) in respect of that relevant offence.

new: If a child is charged before the Court with a designated offence committed when the child was aged 14 years, the Court must not hear and determine the charge summarily unless— (a) the child or the prosecution requests that the charge be heard and determined summarily; and (b) the Court is satisfied that the sentencing options available to it under this Act are adequate to respond to the child's offending; and (c) any of the following applies— (i) it is in the interests of the victim or victims that the charge be heard and determined summarily; (ii) the accused is particularly vulnerable because of cognitive impairment or mental illness; (iii) there is a substantial and compelling reason why the charge should be heard and determined summarily. (7B) In determining whether there is a substantial and compelling reason, under subsection (7A)(c)(iii), why the charge should be heard and determined summarily, the Court must have regard to the intention of Parliament that a charge for a designated offence committed by a child aged 14 years should not normally be heard and determined summarily. new: Indictable offences that must be uplifted—designated offence committed at 14 years of age (1) The Children's Court must not hear and determine summarily a charge against a child for a designated offence committed when the child was 14 years of age unless— (a) the child or the prosecution requests that the charge be heard and determined summarily; and (b) the Court is satisfied that the sentencing options available to it under this Act are adequate to respond to the child's offending; and (c) any of the following applies— (i) it is in the interests of the victim or victims that the charge be heard and determined summarily; (ii) the accused is particularly vulnerable because of a disability or a mental illness; (iii) there is a substantial and compelling reason why the charge should be heard and determined summarily. (2) In determining whether there is a substantial and compelling reason, under subsection (1)(c)(iii), why the charge should be heard and determined summarily, the Children's Court must have regard to the intention of Parliament that a charge for a designated offence committed by a child aged 14 years should not normally be heard and determined summarily. (3) If the child is under 15 years of age and a parent of the child is not present before the Children's Court, the Court may— (a) adjourn the hearing of the proceeding for the purpose of securing a parent's attendance; or (b) hear and determine the proceeding in the absence of a parent. 157B Indictable offences that must be uplifted—carjacking committed at 14 years of age or over (1) The Children's Court must not hear and determine summarily a charge for an offence against section 79 of the Crimes Act 1958 (carjacking) committed by a child who was 14 years of age or over unless— (a) the child or the prosecution requests that the charge be heard and determined summarily; and (b) the Court is satisfied that the sentencing options available to it under this Act are adequate to respond to the child's offending; and (c) any of the following applies— (i) it is in the interests of the victim or victims that the charge be heard and determined summarily; (ii) the accused is particularly vulnerable because of a disability or a mental illness; (iii) there is a substantial and compelling reason why the charge should be heard and determined summarily. (2) In determining whether there is a substantial and compelling reason, under subsection (1)(c)(iii), why the charge should be heard and determined summarily, the Children's Court must have regard to the intention of Parliament that a charge for an offence against section 79 of the Crimes Act 1958 (carjacking) committed when the child was aged 14 years or over should not normally be heard and determined summarily. (3) If the child is under 15 years of age and a parent of the child is not present before the Children's Court, the Court may— (a) adjourn the hearing of the proceeding for the purpose of securing a parent's attendance; or (b) hear and determine the proceeding in the absence of a parent.
